title: Symmetric Kahane--Salem--Zygmund Inequalities and the Supremum Norm
summary: The Kahane--Salem--Zygmund inequality provides unimodular $m$-linear forms with small supremum norm. We consider its dimension-free symmetric constant $C_m^{\mathrm{sym}}$ over the real scalar field, defined by the requirement that, for every $n$, some real symmetric unimodular $m$-linear form $A:(\ell_\infty^n)^m\to\mathbb R$ satisfy \[ \|A\|\le C_m^{\mathrm{sym}}n^{(m+1)/2}. \] For complex scalars, Boas obtained under permutation symmetry an upper bound of order at most $\sqrt{m\log m}\,\sqrt{m!}$; over the real scalar field, an elementary argument gives the sharper order $\sqrt…
